items.title: Results posted for a study of Bimatoprost for Open-Angle Glaucoma
items.summary: AbbVie ran this final-stage test (phase 3) with 515 people. The registry lists its end date as 8 Aug 2025. The study team posted its results on ClinicalTrials.gov. Our search of PubMed and Europe PMC for this study’s number (NCT03850782) found no journal article. Searches can miss articles, so one may already exist. We don’t say here whether the treatment worked. The official study record has the full results.

The registry lists its end date as 24 Sep 2025. The study team posted its results on ClinicalTrials.gov. items.title: A study of ferric citrate for Hyperphosphatemia Related to Chronic Kidney Disease is paused
items.summary: Keryx Biopharmaceuticals leads this final-stage test (phase 3). The study team’s reason: “Sponsor decision”. It may start again. The registry doesn’t say when it was paused. The date above is when its record was last updated.

items.title: A study of Pelacarsen for Hyperlipoproteinemia (a) was stopped early
items.summary: Novartis Pharmaceuticals ran this final-stage test (phase 3) with 41 people. The study team’s reason: “Study terminated by sponsor following the outcome of the Lp(a)HORIZON study (NCT04023552), which did not meet its primary endpoint”. The registry lists its end date as 15 Oct 2026.

items.title: A study of JDQ443 for Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer was stopped early
items.summary: Novartis Pharmaceuticals ran this final-stage test (phase 3) with 95 people. The study team’s reason: “Business reasons and not based on any safety concerns”. The registry lists its end date as 5 Oct 2026.

items.title: A study of Coagadex for Acquired Factor X Deficiency was cancelled before it began
items.summary: Kedrion S.p.A. planned this final-stage test (phase 3). The study team’s reason: “Study was discontinued for non-safety reasons and the rapidly evolving treatment landscape for AL amyloidosis”. The registry doesn’t say when it was cancelled. The date above is when its record was last updated.
